informal: The Lean shows that approximations within \(2\) of \(2^tV\) give exact signed-digit streams with digits in \([-6,6]\), and that recipes built from Lipschitz arithmetic gates, indexed sums and indexed ranks compile to programs emitting such streams within explicit space costs.

results.informal: If \(|V|\le 1\) and \(|N_i-2^iV|\le 2\) for \(i\le H\), the difference digits \(z_t\) satisfy \(|z_t|\le 6\), their weighted partial sums give \(N_H\), and each \(z_t\) is recovered from \(N_t\) and \(N_{t-1}\) modulo \(32\).
results.note: The Lean predicate Checked is the approximation condition (with \(\le 2\)), dsign is the difference digit \(z_t\), and codeQ/diffd recover the digit from residues modulo \(2^5\).

decls.name: safe_d
decls.informal: If \(|V|\le 1\) and \(|N_i-2^iV|\le 2\) for all \(i\le H\), then for \(t\le H\) the digit \(z_t\) (with \(z_0=N_0\), \(z_t=N_t-2N_{t-1}\)) satisfies \(|z_t|\le 6\).

chunks.DyadicArithmetic.safe_d/1: Over the reals \(|z_t|\le 6\): at \(t=0\) from \(|N_0-V|\le 2\) and \(|V|\le 1\), and at \(t+1\) from \(z_{t+1}=(N_{t+1}-2^{t+1}V)-2(N_t-2^tV)\).

decls.name: sumsign
decls.informal: For every integer sequence \(N\) and every \(H\), \(\sum_{i=0}^{H} z_i\,2^{H-i}=N_H\), where \(z_0=N_0\) and \(z_i=N_i-2N_{i-1}\).

results.informal: A program run on a child query \(r=f(q,o)\) can be inlined into a caller with tuple \(q\) that keeps only the short piece \(o\), regenerating \(r\) on demand, with the space allowance enlarged to cost \(g\ge 2C+c\).
results.note: focus_word is the Lean mechanism by which child queries are regenerated from the caller tuple and a small stored piece instead of saved addresses, which is the core of the paper's regenerated-address evaluation.

decls.name: focus_word
decls.informal: If program \(p\) runs from \(a\) to \(y\) at cost \(c\) and clock \(j\) on the query \(r=f(q,o)\), the piece \(o\) satisfies \(\ell(o)+1+Cj\le Ct+C^2d\), \(d\le w\), \(2C+c\le g\) and \(c,C\ge 1\), then the inlined program that regenerates \(r\) from \((q,o)\) runs on query \(q\) from \((o,a)\) to \((o,y)\) at cost \(g\) and clock \(t\).

chunks.RecursivePrograms.focus_word/0: Every state admissible at cost \(c\) and clock \(j\) stays admissible at cost \(g\) and clock \(t\) once paired with \(o\).
chunks.RecursivePrograms.focus_word/1: Every call admissible at cost \(c\) and clock \(j\) stays admissible at cost \(g\) and clock \(t\) once the caller record is paired with \(o\).
chunks.RecursivePrograms.focus_word/1/0: The width condition carries over, and the length bound combines the bounds for \(o\) and for the record.
chunks.RecursivePrograms.focus_word/1/1: The slack \(d\) is at most the caller width minus the callee width.
chunks.RecursivePrograms.focus_word/2: Proceed by induction on the execution of \(p\).
chunks.RecursivePrograms.focus_word/3: For an edit step, the regenerated query gives the same output state, now paired with \(o\).
chunks.RecursivePrograms.focus_word/4: For a call step, the regenerated query gives the same callee query and return state, paired with \(o\).
chunks.RecursivePrograms.focus_word/5: Sequential composition follows from the two induction hypotheses.
chunks.RecursivePrograms.focus_word/6: For a branch taking the true side, the guard on the regenerated query agrees with the original guard.
chunks.RecursivePrograms.focus_word/7: For a branch taking the false side, the guard on the regenerated query agrees with the original guard.
chunks.RecursivePrograms.focus_word/8: For a loop iteration, the guard on the regenerated query is still true, so the iteration carries over.
chunks.RecursivePrograms.focus_word/9: For a loop exit, the guard on the regenerated query is still false and the final state stays admissible.

results.informal: A gate \(F\) that is \(2^{ed}\)-Lipschitz on the operand ranges turns exact operand streams with clock overshoot \((e+i+j+6)d\) into an exact output stream, and each of \(+,-,\times,\min,\max\) and \(x\mapsto 1/\max(x,1)\) is such a gate with \(e=i+j+2\).
results.note: Lean replaces the paper's residue procedures by a generic Lipschitz gate theorem (joint) plus a Lipschitz certificate for the elementary operations (legit), with overshoot linear in the slack \(d\).

decls.name: joint
decls.informal: If \(F\) is exact on rationals and \(2^{ed}\)-Lipschitz for \(|x|\le 2\cdot 2^{id}\), \(|y|\le 2\cdot 2^{jd}\), the operand programs emit exact streams for \(V/2^{id}\) and \(X/2^{jd}\) up to clock \(H+(e+i+j+6)d\), and \(|F(V,X)|\le 2^{od}\), then the combined gate program emits an exact stream for \(F(V,X)/2^{od}\) up to clock \(H\) at cost \(\text{powder}(\text{price}(e+i+j+106+c))\).

chunks.QueryPrograms.joint/1: Fix tapes \(w,b\) for the operand streams and set up the paired recipe with operand values \(V/2^{id}\) and \(X/2^{jd}\).
chunks.QueryPrograms.joint/2: The combined cost \(C\) satisfies \(C\ge 100\) and \(c\le C\).
chunks.QueryPrograms.joint/4: The paired recipe's operand requirements hold up to clock \(H+(e+i+j+6)d\).
chunks.QueryPrograms.joint/4/0: It suffices to check the margin bound, the label counts, and the operand streams.
chunks.QueryPrograms.joint/4/2: Each side has one label and \(1<2^{Cd}\).
chunks.QueryPrograms.joint/4/3: Fix a side and a label, and split on the side.
chunks.QueryPrograms.joint/4/4: On the false side the stream for \(X/2^{jd}\) works.
chunks.QueryPrograms.joint/4/4/1: Raise the cost of the stream for \(X/2^{jd}\) from \(c\) to \(C\).
chunks.QueryPrograms.joint/4/5: On the true side the stream for \(V/2^{id}\) works.
chunks.QueryPrograms.joint/4/5/1: Raise the cost of the stream for \(V/2^{id}\) from \(c\) to \(C\).
chunks.QueryPrograms.joint/5: The gate is Lipschitz with constant \(2^{(e+i+j)d}\) about the target \(F(V,X)/2^{od}\).
chunks.QueryPrograms.joint/5/2: For \(x,y\) within \(1\) of the operand values, the output error is at most \(2^{(e+i+j)d}\) times the sum of the input errors.
chunks.QueryPrograms.joint/5/2/2: The gate output is \(F(x2^{id},y2^{jd})/2^{od}\), so the scaled Lipschitz bound applies.
chunks.QueryPrograms.joint/6: The recipe stream theorem gives the exact output stream.

decls.name: legit
decls.informal: For \(F\in\{+,-,\times,\min,\max,(x,y)\mapsto 1/\max(x,1)\}\), the rational gate computes \(F\) exactly, and for \(d\ge 1\), \(|x|,|z|\le 2\cdot 2^{id}\), \(|y|,|w|\le 2\cdot 2^{jd}\): \(|F(x,y)-F(z,w)|\le 2^{(i+j+2)d}(|x-z|+|y-w|)\).

chunks.QueryPrograms.legit/0: Split into exactness of the rational gate and the Lipschitz bound.
chunks.QueryPrograms.legit/1: In every case the rational gate computes the real operation exactly.
chunks.QueryPrograms.legit/13/3: Write \(xy-zw=(x-z)y+(y-w)z\) and use the triangle inequality.

results.informal: The clipped reciprocal \(x\mapsto 1/\max(x,1)\) is \(1\)-Lipschitz, so it fits the Lipschitz gate interface.
results.note: Lean handles reciprocals only through the clipped gate \(1/\max(x,1)\) (the flip operation), whose Lipschitz bound down_clip replaces the paper's Taylor-based reciprocal on a compact interval.

results.informal: For at most \(2^{ed}\) indexed values with exact streams, the rank program emits an exact stream for the \(k\)-th largest value (clipped at \(0\)), and clipping and ranking exact approximations gives exact approximations of the rank.
results.note: lease states that an indexed order statistic over fewer than \(2^{ed}\) descriptors has an exact digit stream at controlled cost, and sweepV is the approximation bound \(|N_t-2^t\,\text{rank}|\le 2\) behind it.

decls.name: lease
decls.informal: If \(n<2^{ed}\) and each \(V_j\), \(j<n\), has an exact stream for \(V_j/2^{id}\) up to clock \(H\) at cost \(c\ge 1\), then the rank program emits an exact stream for \(\text{rank}_k(V)/2^{id}\) up to clock \(H\) at cost \(\text{powder}(100\,\text{price}(c+e+100))\), where \(\text{rank}_k\) is the zero-based \(k\)-th largest value, padded by \(0\).

chunks.QueryPrograms.lease/1: For each index \(j\) choose a tape that is an exact stream for \(V_j/2^{id}\) whenever \(j<n\).
chunks.QueryPrograms.lease/2: Fix these tapes \(w_j\), the rank recipe, and the normalized values \(W_j=V_j/2^{id}\).
chunks.QueryPrograms.lease/3: The rank recipe's hypotheses hold at cost \(c+e+100\): \(n<2^{(c+e+100)d}\) and each \(w_j\) is an exact stream for \(W_j\).
chunks.QueryPrograms.lease/6: The rank recipe emits an exact stream for \(\text{rank}_k(V)/v\).

decls.name: sweepV
decls.informal: If for each \(i\in S\), \(|V_i|\le 1\) and \(|N^{(i)}_t-2^tV_i|\le 2\) for \(t\le H\), then \(t\mapsto \text{rank}_k\big(\max(N^{(i)}_t,0)\big)\) satisfies the same condition for \(\text{rank}_k(V)\).

chunks.DyadicArithmetic.sweepV/1: \(|\text{rank}_k(V)|\le 1\) since all \(V_i\le 1\), and it remains to fix \(t\le H\).
chunks.DyadicArithmetic.sweepV/2: Since rank is \(2\)-Lipschitz in the sup norm, \(|\text{rank}_k(N_t)-\text{rank}_k(2^tV)|\le 2\).
chunks.DyadicArithmetic.sweepV/3: \(\max(0,N^{(i)}_t)\) equals the value of \(N^{(i)}_t\) clipped to a natural number.
chunks.DyadicArithmetic.sweepV/4: Rank is unchanged by clipping at \(0\) and scales by \(2^t\), so \(|\text{rank}_k(\max(N_t,0))-2^t\,\text{rank}_k(V)|\le 2\).

results.informal: For fewer than \(2^{ed}\) terms with exact streams at clock overshoot \((e+6)d\), the sum program emits an exact stream for the sum rescaled by \(2^{-(i+e)d}\).
results.note: poem states the bounded indexed sum with the known scale \(2^{ed}\) absorbing the term count, with an \(O(d)\) clock overshoot, matching the paper's bounded sums and known scales.

decls.name: poem
decls.informal: If \(n<2^{ed}\) and each \(V_j\), \(j<n\), has an exact stream for \(V_j/2^{id}\) up to clock \(H+(e+6)d\) at cost \(c\ge 1\), then the sum program emits an exact stream for \(\big(\sum_{j<n}V_j\big)/2^{(i+e)d}\) up to clock \(H\) at cost \(\text{powder}(\text{price}(c+e+106))\).

chunks.QueryPrograms.poem/0: Set up the sum recipe, the cost \(C=c+e+106\), the weight \(o=i+e\), \(D=2^{id}\) and \(B=2^{od}\).
chunks.QueryPrograms.poem/5: Each side of the recipe has at most \(n\) labels.
chunks.QueryPrograms.poem/6: For each side and label \(j\), choose a tape that is an exact stream for \(W_j\) up to \(H+(e+6)d\) whenever \(j\) is a valid label.
chunks.QueryPrograms.poem/6/0: Split on whether \(j\) is a valid label.
chunks.QueryPrograms.poem/6/1: If it is, take the given stream.
chunks.QueryPrograms.poem/9: The sum recipe's operand requirements hold at cost \(C\).
chunks.QueryPrograms.poem/9/0: The margin satisfies \((e+6)d\le Cd\), leaving the label counts and the streams.
chunks.QueryPrograms.poem/9/1: Each label count is at most \(n<2^{ed}\le 2^{Cd}\).
chunks.QueryPrograms.poem/9/2: Each operand stream is raised to cost \(C\).
chunks.QueryPrograms.poem/14: The sum recipe is \(1\)-Lipschitz about the target \(v/B\).
chunks.QueryPrograms.poem/14/0: It suffices to show \(|v/B|\le 1\), the rate condition, and the error bound.
chunks.QueryPrograms.poem/14/3: The tally of the normalized terms is \(v/D\).
chunks.QueryPrograms.poem/14/4: The gate output is \(xD/B\), so it suffices to show \(|xD/B-v/B|\le |x-v/D|\).
chunks.QueryPrograms.poem/14/6: Since \(0\le D/B\le 1\), the error is at most \(|x-v/D|\).
chunks.QueryPrograms.poem/15: The recipe stream theorem gives the exact output stream.

results.informal: A test program reads the operand approximation at clock \(t=md\), evaluates a fixed test on the value \(2^{id}N_t/2^t\), which is within \(2^{id}\cdot 2/2^t\) of \(V\), and returns its result from clock \(0\).
results.note: Badge (docstring: probe an actual finite-margin numerical question) queries one operand at an \(O(d)\) clock and evaluates a finite test whose result does not depend on an output clock; the specific \(s>2u\) versus \(s>u\) guarantee is not stated here.

decls.name: query
decls.informal: If the operand program emits an exact stream \(N\) for \(V/2^{id}\) up to clock \(t=md\) at cost \(c\ge 1\), and \(j\) is the test result on \(2^{id}N_t/2^t\) with \(\ell(j)+1\le cd\), then the check program, started from \(0\) at clock \(0\), outputs \(j\) at cost \(4\,\text{price}(c+m+100)\).

chunks.QueryPrograms.query/0: Use the one-operand recipe and set \(c_1=c+m+100\).
chunks.QueryPrograms.query/3: The one-operand recipe's hypotheses hold at cost \(c_1\) and clock \(t\).
chunks.QueryPrograms.query/3/0: It remains to bound the label counts and supply the operand stream.
chunks.QueryPrograms.query/3/1: Each side has at most one label and \(1<2^{c_1d}\).
chunks.QueryPrograms.query/3/1/0: Each side has at most one label.
chunks.QueryPrograms.query/3/1/2: Hence the label count is below \(2^{c_1d}\).
chunks.QueryPrograms.query/3/2: The operand stream at cost \(c\) is raised to cost \(c_1\).
chunks.QueryPrograms.query/4: Running the recipe reaches its finished state.
chunks.QueryPrograms.query/6: Started from \(0\), the recipe reaches the record \(v\) at clock \(t\).
chunks.QueryPrograms.query/8: Dispatching to clock \(t=md\), the first phase runs from clock \(0\) to the record \(v\) at cost \(4\,\text{price}(c_1)\).
chunks.QueryPrograms.query/9: Compose with the final step that evaluates the test on \(v\), leaving its value and space bounds.
chunks.QueryPrograms.query/10/1: So the tested value is \(2^{id}N_t/2^t\), whose test result is \(j\).

decls.name: accuracy
decls.informal: If \(|V/2^{id}|\le 1\) and \(|N_s-2^sV/2^{id}|\le 2\) for \(s\le t\), then \(x=2^{id}N_t/2^t\) satisfies \(|x-V|\le 2^{id}\cdot 2/2^t\).

results.informal: Every recipe built from base streams, the gates \(+,-,\times,\min,\max,1/\max(\cdot,1)\), indexed sums and indexed ranks compiles to a program that emits an exact stream for its value scaled by \(2^{-\text{weight}\cdot d}\), at a cost determined by the recipe, provided operands are valid \(\text{tail}\cdot d\) clocks beyond the output clock.
results.note: song is proved by induction over the recipe class Lyric (base streams, Doop gates, indexed sums and ranks), combining joint, poem and lease, which is the paper's uniform numerical interface.

decls.name: song
decls.informal: If a recipe \(f\) has value \(V\) with all its operands valid up to clock \(T\), \(c\ge 1\), and \(H+\text{tail}(f)\,d\le T\), then the compiled program emits an exact stream for \(V/2^{\text{weight}(f)d}\) up to clock \(H\) at cost \(\text{cost}(f,c)\).

decls.name: Lethe.bnd
decls.informal: If a recipe \(f\) has value \(V\), then \(|V|\le 2^{\text{weight}(f)d}\).

unmapped.reason: Lean has no separate band-multiplication procedure; products are computed exactly on rational approximations and covered by the multiplication case of the Lipschitz gate lemma.
Remark about how clocks are used; it has no separate Lean statement.
